name: issue_1066_breach_ignores_dwell_lock
description: The 600 s anti-chatter dwell lock applies only to NON-breach switches. Mild day, band 68F/74F, margin 2F. A non-breach switch to cool at 08:00 starts the clock; a non-breach flip back to heat 300 s later is held; a breach below the floor (67F) 360 s after the switch is commanded immediately (heat) because comfort protection overrides anti-chatter; a following non-breach flip to cool 240 s later is held again (the breach restarted the clock), and is applied only once 600 s have elapsed (08:17).
source: Issue #1066 plan, dwell-lock semantics (docs/08 section 6f 'Reactive evaluation, dwell lock, decision memory')
notes: Occupant impact: the house is never left below its comfort floor (or above the ceiling) just because the HVAC switched modes a few minutes ago, yet it also does not flip modes every few minutes while hovering at the boundaries.

The locked_out events come from the scheduled classification cycle (the reactive temperature path stays silent while the lock would block the switch), so each non-breach step also carries a classification event at the same timestamp.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: on origin/main the family switch required breach + deadband + 90 s sustain, and cool-to-heat at 70F (no breach) was impossible, so the 08:05 locked_out(heating) assertion could never be met; the 08:06 breach switch landing without waiting for the sustain window (event at 08:06 with breach=true) would also fail. If the new FSM did not let breaches bypass the lock, the 08:06 switch would be locked_out instead and the breach assertion would fail; if the lock were removed, the 08:05 and 08:10 locked_out assertions would fail.

(b) Docs vs production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f 'A non-breach switch within comfort_mode_switch_min_interval_s ... is held; a breach switch always proceeds and restarts the clock. The clock moves only on a genuine transition.'

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: either the house stays below its floor for up to ten minutes after a recent mode switch, or the HVAC short-cycles between heat and cool at the band boundaries.
Classification fields: day_type=mild, hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=true with 10:00/17:00 window times match classifier.py for DAY_TYPE_MILD.

events.note: Indoor 69F in the heat zone; thermostat in heat. Baseline.
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: Indoor 69F in the heat zone; thermostat in heat. Baseline.
72.5F reaches ceiling-m: non-breach switch to cool (the transition that starts the 600 s dwell clock).
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: 72.5F reaches ceiling-m: non-breach switch to cool (the transition that starts the 600 s dwell clock).
70F reaches floor+m only 300 s after the switch: a NON-breach flip back to heat is held by the dwell lock (comfort_family_switch_locked_out).
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: 70F reaches floor+m only 300 s after the switch: a NON-breach flip back to heat is held by the dwell lock (comfort_family_switch_locked_out).
67F is below the 68F floor: a BREACH. Heat is armed immediately even though only 360 s have passed since the cool switch.
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: 67F is below the 68F floor: a BREACH. Heat is armed immediately even though only 360 s have passed since the cool switch.
73F wants cool, but this is a non-breach flip 240 s after the 08:06 breach transition (which restarted the clock): held again.
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: 73F wants cool, but this is a non-breach flip 240 s after the 08:06 breach transition (which restarted the clock): held again.
72F: 660 s after the 08:06 transition the lock has expired, so the non-breach flip to cool is finally applied.
Evaluation cycle at the same reading: 72F: 660 s after the 08:06 transition the lock has expired, so the non-breach flip to cool is finally applied.

assertions.reason: Non-breach switch to cool at ceiling-m starts the dwell clock.
A non-breach flip back to heat 300 s after the switch is delayed: the FSM emits locked_out (candidate heating) instead of switching.
A breach below the floor is commanded immediately, ignoring the 600 s lock (only 360 s since the cool switch).
The breach restarted the dwell clock, so a non-breach flip to cool 240 s later is locked out (candidate cooling).
Once 660 s have passed since the last genuine transition the delayed non-breach flip to cool is applied.
Final family cooling after the lock expired.

verdict.summary: Breaches bypass the 600 s dwell lock; non-breach flips inside it are delayed until it expires.
verdict.observed_behavior: Locked out at 08:05 and 08:10, breach heat at 08:06, delayed cool applied at 08:17.
